messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert triggered for NET-4923 — elevated 5xx from edge services in eu-west-1 (azd). Auto-signal: route53 latency spikes + ELB target health flaps. Paging @Maya (primary on-call), @Sam (network). Incident created: https://pagerduty.example/INC4923 :rotating_light:
Maya: Acknowledged. I'm on call. First glance: synthetic checks show 502/503s hitting the ALB from health checks and client traffic.
Sam: I'm seeing similar from our external probes — traceroutes show increased hop delays leaving azd. Could be an AZ-specific egress path issue.
Keerthi: Adding context — we rolled a config change to gateway-proxy in azd ~2h ago but it was limited canary. I don't think it's configwide.
Maya: Ok, let's validate Route53. Running dig and curl from control plane:
```
$ dig +short www.redwood.example @8.8.8.8
54.239.28.85
$ dig +trace redwood.example
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> +trace redwood.example
;; Received 2000 bytes from 203.0.113.5#53(203.0.113.5) in 85 ms
;; Received 2000 bytes from 198.51.100.6#53(198.51.100.6) in 310 ms
```
Maya: trace shows some authoritative responses taking 300ms+ for azd-backed NS.
Sam: curl against ALB from outside: `curl -i https://api.redwood.example/v1/health` returns 503 with `x-elb-health: degraded`.
Keerthi: Pulling ELB metrics — target group in azd shows targets toggling Unhealthy/Healthy around minute boundaries. CPU and memory on targets are fine. No obvious app-level OOM.
Raj: Could be network-level packet drops causing TCP resets -> ELB marks targets unhealthy. Any ENI/container restarts?
Maya: Checked ECS task history: no restarts. Docker logs for gateway-proxy show increased backend connection timeouts: `dial tcp x.x.x.x:443: i/o timeout`.
Sam: I ran `mtr` from an edge probe into azd, path shows a node with consistent 20-40% packet loss between two transit routers in the AZ's egress path.
OpsBot: Incident runbook NET-OUT-001 recommended steps: 1) isolate AZ, 2) shift traffic via weighted Route53 failover, 3) engage cloud-provider support.
Maya: Step 1: Can we shift traffic off azd? We use Route53 weighted routing with per-AZ records. If we update weights, traffic will re-route in ~TTL window. TTL for our apex is 60s — good.
Keerthi: I can adjust Route53 weight and lower azd weight to 0, move weight to azc/aze. Suggest: update records for api.redwood.example weight: azd=0, azc=70, aze=30.
Daniel: I'll prepare the change. Note: we also have inter-region fallback (eu-west-2) but prefer intra-region AZ shift first.
Maya: Before we shift, we should put the azd targets into draining on the ALB to avoid mid-request failures. Keerthi, can you set target group deregistration delay to 30s and mark instances draining?
Keerthi: Doing `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <arn> --targets Id=i-0abc...` for the azd targets now.
Maya: Confirmed. Traffic to azd targets decreasing, ALB health checks still occasionally failing but connection attempts dropping.
Sam: Route53 weight change going out in 10s. Doing via console to be atomic.
Daniel: Change applied: azd=0, azc=80, aze=20. Route53 cached TTL 60s — we should see inbound traffic shift within 90s.
Maya: Monitoring metrics: canary probes to /v1/health returning 200s from azc/aze. Overall edge 5xx rate dropping.
Raj: Noted some customer sessions still routed to azd due to client-side caching — might continue for up to TTL.
Maya: I'm opening an AWS support case for potential AZ egress packet loss and providing packet capture traces and mtr output. Case: 1234567890.
Sam: AWS responded: "We see a noisy transit node affecting egress from azd, working on mitigation." ETA unknown.
OpsBot: Severity set to SEV-2. Customer impact: degraded latency and 10-15% request failures for small subset of customers in EU region.
Maya: Initiating customer comms draft: "We are experiencing a regional networking degradation in eu-west-1 AZ-D affecting some API requests. Traffic has been rerouted to healthy AZs and recovery is in progress. We will provide updates every 30 minutes."
Keerthi: Updating runbook note: mark configuration canary paused until further notice. Will revert canary rollout after full recovery and postmortem.
Sam: Quick mitigation note — for long-lived websocket connections pinned to azd, we may need to force disconnect and reconnect to ensure clients failover to healthy AZs. Maya, can you coordinate with SDK team for a graceful reconnect?
Maya: On it. Pushing an advisory to the push-router to emit 1001 reconnect for pinned connections in azd.
Daniel: We're seeing ingress error rates back down to baseline across region except residual 0.5% from legacy edge nodes.
Maya: Handing off to @Sam for next 2hr watch. I'll update postmortem checklist and switch to notes.
Sam: Taking over watch. I'm staying on the incident channel. AWS case updated with captures. If we see another spike, we'll consider full-region failover to eu-west-2 as escalation.
Raj: Adding a note: check EBS detach logs in azd if any IO stalls coincide — weird I/O spikes could cause connection stalls though no detach events seen so far.
Maya: Snapshots and EBS health looked stable. No elevated I/O wait on instances.
OpsBot: Next update scheduled +30m. Incident status: mitigated (traffic shifted), monitoring.
Sam: Leaving a short triage action list: 1) AWS support follow-up and packet trace analysis, 2) revert Route53 weights once AWS confirms fix and all target groups stable for 15m, 3) run canonical synthetic sweep + perf runbook, 4) create follow-up postmortem.
Daniel: I'll create the postmortem ticket and assign owners.
Maya: Thanks team. I've also added a customer-impact list to the incident ticket (10 enterprise customers with some requests failing). Outreach queued.
Sam: Closing paging window. Handing to follow-up rotation. If we see recurrence, re-open incident channel. :white_check_mark:
IncidentBot: Incident NET-4923 status updated to MONITORED. Logs archived to s3://incidents/NET-4923/ and Slack thread persisted.
